items.title: At TomorrowX, I listened to Lisa Su of AMD $AMD, Michael Dell of Dell $DELL, David Solomon of Goldman Sachs $GS, Jitendra Mohan of Astera Labs $ALAB and others. I didn’t catch ever
items.body: At TomorrowX, I listened to Lisa Su of AMD $AMD, Michael Dell of Dell $DELL, David Solomon of Goldman Sachs $GS, Jitendra Mohan of Astera Labs $ALAB and others. I didn’t catch every session, but the conversations I heard were largely focused on the long-term promise of technology. I share that optimism. The computing ecosystem Jensen Huang and NVIDIA $NVDA helped build has made today’s AI and infrastructure possible. I believe it can also help improve lives through drug discovery, cancer treatment and more. The potential downsides of AI were even addressed in Korea’s recent college entrance exam. Those concerns are real. But I hope we can move beyond fear and find ways for technology and policy to work together so that more people can benefit. The TomorrowX opening video has stayed with me. It traced humanity’s journey from the rise of civilization and the invention of the wheel to the steam engine, semiconductors, GPUs and AI. People have surely feared new technologies before. Yet we have also used them to build better lives. AI is another tool in that journey. What matters is how we use it to benefit humanity and help people live better, more peaceful lives. Investing, however, is a different question. Stanley Druckenmiller said he wouldn’t dare short equities with so much innovation underway. But he also couldn’t remember a period when he had less clarity about where things would stand in 12 months. For now, he’s focused on preserving capital and mostly staying away from equities. “I play big when I’m hot, when I’m cold I do little bunts.” My own gains have fallen significantly from their peak. I’m still excited about the future of technology, but honestly, I’m not sure what to do with my portfolio right now. When even Druckenmiller is sitting much of it out, you realize how difficult this market really is.

external_articles.title: HBM4 가격, 내년 2배 껑충…삼성·SK AI 메모리 사업 '청신호'
external_articles.body:
HBM4, 올해 Gb당 2.05달러 이상…내년 3~5.5달러로 상승 전망

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/11/18 13:30    수정: 2026/11/18 14:07

내년 주류 제품인 HBM4(6세대 HBM)의 경우 Gb(기가비트) 당 가격은 올해 2.05 달러 이상에서 내년 3~5.5 달러대를 형성할 것으로 예상된다. 전년 대비 2배 이상의 성장세다.

글로벌 IT시장조사 및 컨설팅 기업인 트렌드포스는 18일 서울 오크우드 프리미어 코엑스 센터에서 '2026 로드쇼 코리아' 행사를 열고 메모리반도체 시장 전망에 대해 이같이 밝혔다.

엘리 왕 트렌드포스 수석연구원은 "중국 YMTC의 공격적인 생산능력 확대로 낸드 가격은 내년 2분기부터 하락세로 돌아설 것"이라며 "반면 D램은 내년까지 가격이 하락 전환하지 않을 것으로 판단한다"고 말했다.

트렌드포스가 전망한 올 4분기 범용 D램의 평균판매가격 상승률은 전분기 대비 10~15% 수준이다. 이후 내년 ▲1분기 5~10% ▲2분기 3~8% ▲3분기 0~5% ▲4분기 0~5%로 완만하게 상승할 것으로 예상된다.

최근 일부 제품의 현물가격이 하락하는 등 변동성은 존재하지만, 제품 전반의 가격 상승은 지속될 것이라는 해석이다.

HBM 가격도 동반 상승한다. HBM4 기준 Gb당 가격은 올해 2.05 달러 이상에서 내년 3~5.5 달러로 전년 대비 100% 이상 증가할 전망이다. 차세대 제품인 HBM4E는 5달러 이상으로 논의되고 있다. 내년 상반기께 구체화될 예정이다.

D램 및 HBM 시장이 낸드 대비 비교적 견고한 이유는 공급 측면에 있다. 먼저 중국 최대 D램 제조기업인 CXMT의 생산능력이 올해 월 3만장 수준에서 내년 월 3만6000장 수준으로 제한적인 성장세를 보일 전망이다.

현지 고객사들이 GPU 등 고성능 시스템반도체 수급 난항으로 AI 인프라를 적극 확충하지 못하고 있어서다. 최근 미국 정부는 중국향 AI 반도체 우회접근은 물론 수출 규제 수위를 지속 강화하고 있다.

HBM 공급 확대에 따른 범용 D램 출하량 축소 압박도 주요 원인 중 하나다. HBM은 높은 제조 난이도로 범용 D램 대비 웨이퍼 소모량이 약 3~4배 많다. 삼성전자·SK하이닉스·마이크론 등 주요 메모리 기업 3사의 전체 D램 웨이퍼에서 HBM이 차지하는 비중은 올해 23%에서 내년 30%에 육박할 것으로 관측된다.

다만 2028년은 다양한 변수로 인해 시장의 불확실성이 높다. 해당 시점부터 삼성전자, SK하이닉스, CXMT 등 주요 D램 제조기업의 신규 D램 생산능력이 대폭 늘어난다. 미국 민주당의 중간선거 압승으로 2028년 이후의 데이터센터 구축 계획이 지연될 가능성도 거론되고 있다.

엘리 왕 연구원은 "삼성전자 P5의 페이즈(Ph)1, 2가 각각 월 20만장 규모로 구축될 예정이고, SK하이닉스 역시 용인 반도체 클러스터에서 월 30만장의 생산능력을 확보하려고 한다"며 "CXMT는 2028년 이후 월 10만~20만장 규모의 추가 증설을 추진 중"이라고 말했다.

The purpose of this session was to run through the dos and don'ts; more importantly, the professionalism and behavior expected at this event, especially of those who may be selected for breakouts, given the lineup of speakers iirc, he emphasized on "respect" several times I could tell that Gavin was bordering on anticipatory anxiety. Dread and worry, even I can totally understand why, judging by how some popular FinX personalities behave on X - puerile, disrespectful, even mocking company executives by name, tagging their handles. Many of them hide behind an alias (look, that thinly veiled anonymity is gone with this event) I get that being humans, we can be emotionally charged sometimes due to differing POVs/opinions, but i think we need to be respectful to others offline and online. Some of the stuff I see posted here really put me off It's not about age (or maybe it is), but maturity One doesn't need to be the loudest, or rudest, to get the attention in the room The TomorrowX event is a huge undertaking. We should all be grateful that Gavin and his partners are doing this

items.title: Let’s step in the Time Machine and go back to another crazy period, Feb 2025. DeepSeek drops R1, trained for peanuts (supposedly), NVDA loses $600Bn in a day, and everyone says eff
items.body: Let’s step in the Time Machine and go back to another crazy period, Feb 2025. DeepSeek drops R1, trained for peanuts (supposedly), NVDA loses $600Bn in a day, and everyone says efficiency just killed the AI stars. The entire world had maybe ~15 GW ish of AI compute at the time. And since then all the fears came true: the cost of doing the same hard task fell ~99% and cost per token at fixed capability fell 10x a year. Effective compute is up something like 15x by end of this year. By the bear logic nobody should have been building anything from that moment on given the ‘supply monsoon’ from stacked compute and efficiency. Meanwhile here we are on the verge of ANT’s public market debut, a co that went from a $1B run rate to $81B in 19 months and is potentially on its way to ~$150+ in 2027. We literally ran this exact compute supply experiment just under two years ago and are living in the results. So, are we finally overbuilding? The prices certainly suggest that! Or do the price setters have trouble w/ exponentials? We’ll know soon enough... Back to the Red Room for me.

items.body: JUST IN: TSMC says Lam Research’s new Taiwan lab will let their engineers work together earlier on next-generation GAA processes. external_articles.title: 台積電米玉傑：半導體創新不能單打獨鬥 攜科林搶攻GAA下一世代製程 | 政經焦點 | 要聞 | 經濟日報
external_articles.body:
AI引領全球半導體新一波技術革命，先進製程競爭也從單一企業的技術突破，轉向整體產業生態系的協同創新。台積電執行副總經理暨共同營運長米玉傑今（18）日出席美商科林研發（Lam Research）位於苗栗竹南的台灣科技中心動土典禮時強調，隨著半導體結構日趨複雜，創新早已不是任何一家企業能夠獨力完成，設備、材料、晶圓製造及設計夥伴的緊密合作，重要性前所未有。台積電期待透過科林研發新技術中心，深化雙方合作，加速先進製程開發，為GAA（環繞式閘極）時代打造下一世代半導體技術。

今日動土典禮冠蓋雲集，包括台積電研發副總經理章勳明、南亞科總經理李培瑛、苗栗縣長鍾東錦、科林研發台灣主管郭偉毅，以及國科會、經濟部、國家實驗研究院、新竹科學園區管理局、台灣美國商會、科學園區同業公會等政府與產業界代表出席，共同見證科林研發擴大在台研發布局的重要里程碑。

米玉傑指出，數十年來，半導體產業透過電晶體架構創新、製程微縮及系統整合，持續推動科技快速進步。如今人工智慧正引領下一波科技革命，對運算效能及運算能力提出更高要求，半導體產業必須同步推進先進製程、新世代電晶體架構、先進封裝及3D系統整合，才能滿足AI快速成長的需求。

他強調，隨著半導體技術日益複雜，從晶圓製造、設備、材料到IC設計，每個環節都至關重要。唯有透過產業鏈持續深化合作，才能加速技術開發與實驗、縮短學習曲線，並將研發成果轉化為高品質且具備量產能力的製程技術。

米玉傑表示，台積電與科林研發在台灣已攜手合作數十年，雙方合作橫跨多個半導體技術世代。無論是在蝕刻、沉積技術的工程執行，或量產製程的技術開發，科林研發始終是台積電長期信賴的重要合作夥伴。

此次科林研發擴大台灣研發布局，將頂尖研發能量帶到更接近客戶的第一線，讓雙方專家團隊能在技術開發初期就展開深度合作，共同迎接前瞻製程及新世代電晶體架構的挑戰。

科林研發規劃新科技中心於2028年啟用，辦公室與無塵室總面積超過4萬平方公尺，屆時在台整體無塵室產能將擴大至原有9倍以上，研發領域涵蓋沉積、蝕刻及濕式清洗，支援邏輯晶片、記憶體與先進封裝技術。

業界認為，隨著GAA架構及3D整合技術持續演進，半導體設備與製程開發的整合難度同步提高。科林研發將研發資源直接部署在台積電等重要客戶附近，有助縮短設備驗證及新製程開發週期，也凸顯台灣在全球先進半導體技術創新體系中的關鍵地位。

台積電執行副總經理暨共同營運長米玉傑今日出席美商科林研發（Lam Research）位於苗栗竹南的台灣科技中心動土典禮時強調，半導體創新不能單打獨鬥！攜手科林研發搶攻GAA下一世代製程。記者簡永祥／攝影

items.title: https://t.co/CYB0vM0mmQ TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/17/26 Huang spoke for himself for the first time since resigning, owning the personal mistakes
items.body: https://t.co/CYB0vM0mmQ TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/17/26 Huang spoke for himself for the first time since resigning, owning the personal mistakes and saying he would return if the board decided it was best. Hours later the board chair answered on the earnings call: the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, and a search firm is retained. The Wall Street Journal reported a new SEC investigation into whether Nvidia disclosures misled investors. The board created a national security and export control oversight committee. Earnings beat and guidance rose, with no 10-Q filed with the release. The December House interview dates are now reported as agreed, and Muddy Waters disclosed a short with an expressly unverified identity question at its center. HUANG SPEAKS, THE BOARD ANSWERS • Jensen Huang issued his first public statement since resigning as Nvidia CEO, in his own post on November 17, 2026, read in full. He said verbatim: "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation." • He thanked supporters, noted an outpouring of calls from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers for him to return as CEO, and stated: "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." No prior claim in the record records any public statement by Huang himself since the resignation; the comeback reporting was third party. • Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones opened the third quarter earnings call on the evening of November 17, 2026 by stating on the record: "On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." The statement was carried verbatim or near verbatim the same evening by CNN, Engadget, USA Today and Reuters, all read in full; no full earnings call transcript was obtained. • Jones and interim CEO Colette Kress declined to take questions on Huang's resignation or the ongoing investigation, saying the board will communicate further when appropriate. Jones said the board had retained Heidrick and Struggles to lead the permanent CEO search, considering internal and external candidates, thoroughly and as quickly as possible without expediting past the right person, and expressed the board's full confidence in Kress. • This hardens the position in the record: the board's no return position was previously carried only as anonymous sourced reporting on November 16. The chair has now stated it himself, on the record, unanimously, hours after Huang put the return decision to the board. A NEW SEC PROBE • The Wall Street Journal reported on November 17, 2026 that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, according to people familiar with the matter. This is the Journal's reporting, on a single source chain, with no SEC statement, filing or comment recorded and Nvidia not quoted responding. • The Journal describes a civil investigation whose focus could not immediately be learned but includes whether the company's disclosures misled investors, in the wake of Huang's resignation. It notes Nvidia had denied earlier this year that Huang had an unusual or unexpected relationship with Alice Huang, then an executive at Singapore based Megaspeed, and that Nvidia last year changed how it discloses international chip sales, eliminating the disclosure that showed its sales to Singapore. • Reuters Breakingviews the same evening carried the probe as the Wall Street Journal reported. No prior claim in the record records any SEC inquiry; the investigation prongs in the record were Commerce and the Bureau of Industry and Security, the Justice Department and the FBI, Singapore authorities, the board probe and Congress. This opens a new federal prong aimed at investor disclosures, including the earlier denial concerning Alice Huang. THE BOARD BUILDS ITS OVERSIGHT • Nvidia announced on November 17, 2026, in the company's own release, that its board has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, a new standing board committee responsible for board level oversight of the company's national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management. Reuters and TechCrunch carried the announcement the same day with identical particulars. • The committee is chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, with directors Stephen Neal and John Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly, including in executive session, and retain independent outside experts. Nvidia's National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to the committee, with interim CEO Colette Kress overseeing day to day operations. Reuters notes Nvidia did not have a chief compliance officer according to its 2026 proxy statement. • Chair Harvey Jones said: "We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation." No prior claim records this committee; it is the board's first structural governance act on the export control prong since the resignation. The announcement was made on the morning of November 17. EARNINGS LAND, THE 10-Q WAITS • Nvidia reported third quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17, 2026, for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, its first report since Huang's resignation, in a release and CFO commentary carried the same evening by CNN, Engadget, USA Today and Reuters, all read in full: revenue $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year and 20% sequentially, against about $109.1 billion expected and the company's own $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, guide; data center revenue $107.6 billion; GAAP gross margin 74.8%; diluted EPS $2.70, adjusted $2.68. • Fourth quarter guidance: revenue $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, with the quarter including an additional week, gross margin 71.0% to 72.0%, assuming no Data Center compute revenue from China. On the call Kress raised expected fiscal 2028 revenue growth to about 75% year over year, from 70%. Kress also said the company earned $2.4 billion in sales of licensed chips to China during the third quarter and has ceased such shipments. • Nvidia did not file its Form 10-Q with the earnings release. Multiple same evening analyses of the release and CFO commentary state the company said it will file the full 10-Q in the coming weeks and has posted a supplemental financial packet on its investor site in the meantime, a break from its recent pattern of filing the same day as earnings; the analyses note the filing is not late until early December. This timing point is reported at low confidence: the CFO commentary itself was not read firsthand, and the timing rests on relay analyses of it. The speculation in those posts about why is not carried here. THE HOUSE DATES ARE SET • Reporting on November 17, 2026 states the December House dates are now agreed appearances: Jensen Huang will sit for the closed door transcribed interview with the three House committees, Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and the Select Committee on China, on December 1, 2026, and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter will sit for his transcribed interview on December 2, 2026. This is reported, carried by multiple outlets reporting the chairs' joint statement; the joint statement itself was not read firsthand. • The reporting states Huang agreed to appear voluntarily on Tuesday, November 17, in the chairmen's joint statement, and that CNN's November 17 report states Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. The same reporting states the Senate Banking dates, Huang on December 3 and Lutnick on December 10, remain requests with the subpoena warning still standing; a relay post attributing a Senate Banking agreement to Politico is not corroborated by any source read in this window and is not carried as agreed. • No prior claim set these dates: the record had Moolenaar's November 15 confirmation that Huang had agreed to come in, with exact dates still being discussed and the December 1 date expressly not locked. MUDDY WATERS GOES SHORT • Muddy Waters Research disclosed on November 17, 2026 that it is short Nvidia, in its own post titled "MW is Short NVIDIA: More Questions About China", read in full. The short disclosure and the question as posed are verified firsthand from the firm's own post. • The post's substance is a question, stated as such by the firm itself: a woman identified as Cenly Chen, referred to in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, has been photographed in public between 2024 and 2026 with Ajay K. Puri, who until June 2026 was Nvidia's EVP Worldwide Field Operations, described by the firm as likely the third most senior executive at Nvidia, behind only Jensen Huang and Colette Kress, and who continues as a senior adviser. • Separately, an October 2026 consolidated class action complaint against Super Micro Computer alleges that its former Chief Growth Officer, a woman named Cenly Chen, managed Super Micro's acquisition of GPU chips from Nvidia and decided how to distribute Nvidia GPUs among Super Micro's customers, and that there was no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge of Super Micro's illicit sales; in March 2026 the United States indicted three individuals associated with Super Micro, including a co founder, over at least approximately $2.5 billion of Super Micro servers with Nvidia GPUs allegedly sold to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company. • Muddy Waters states expressly: "Nobody by the name of Cenly Chen has been indicted or otherwise accused of criminal conduct by any government. The allegations in the class action are unproven." The question it poses is whether the woman photographed with Puri is the same Cenly Chen formerly employed by Super Micro. That identity is unverified, by the firm's own framing, and nothing here asserts it. Ajay Puri and Cenly Chen are new persons entering the matter through this item. SINGAPORE, BY THE SUBSIDIARY • As carried by an aggregator's summary of Financial Times reporting on November 17, 2026, Nvidia's Singapore subsidiary booked $104 billion in external revenue in 2025, up 72%, representing nearly half of Nvidia's global sales, and Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore linked revenue after changing its geographic reporting methodology from customer billing addresses to headquarters locations, with Nvidia's position that most Singapore billed products were shipped elsewhere. The Financial Times piece itself was not read in this window, so the $104 billion figure is relay grade and unverified at low confidence until the original is read. • The methodology change itself is already in the record from November 11 reporting and is not new here; the new element is the subsidiary scale figure. That figure is a company revenue figure for the Singapore subsidiary, not one of the tracked chip figures, and is not merged with any of them. THE CHECKPOINTS • November 18, 2026: the closed door briefing. • November 24, 2026: Bennet's answers due. • About November 25, 2026: Bessent's 10 day deadline for answers from Nvidia's board and outside counsel. • December 1, 2026: Huang's closed door transcribed interview with the three House committees, now reported as agreed, and the House Foreign Affairs Democrats' answ

external_articles.title: Jensengate | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
The fall of Jensen Huang at Nvidia, tracked in twelve-hour editions: the newest edition in full at the top, and every earlier edition in the archive below.

TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10AM TO 10PM on 11/18/26

Congress widened on every front in this window. A fourth House committee, Energy and Commerce, sent oversight letters to Nvidia and to Commerce leadership with a December 2 briefing deadline. At the Aspen Cyber Summit, a Select Committee member publicly called for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to go, and three House Democrats opened an inquiry into whether the Secretary's family firm interests influenced the decision to keep Megaspeed off the Entity List. Inside Nvidia, the Wall Street Journal's account of an employee letter to the full board arguing that irreplaceable talent is contemplating departing was filed as a catch-up, employees met in the first all-hands since the resignation, and Nvidia's quarterly lobbying disclosure set a record. The November 18 closed door briefing produced no public readout in this window.

The board story split in this window. Semafor reported that a minority faction of Nvidia directors is still pushing to bring Jensen Huang back, one day after the chair stated on the record that the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott confirmed on air that Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have both agreed to appear before his committee, with no date set. The Information placed Nvidia's longtime sales chief, Jay Puri, in direct customer relations with Alice Huang, identified the Cenly Chen in the Muddy Waters photograph question as Puri's wife and a former longtime Super Micro senior executive, and reported that Nvidia's own sales team introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang twice in 2022. Reuters documented a proxy access route by which Huang can nominate two directors. A filings based analysis put hard dates on the delayed Form 10-Q.

Huang spoke for himself for the first time since resigning, owning the personal mistakes and saying he would return if the board decided it was best. Hours later the board chair answered on the earnings call: the board unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, and a search firm is retained. The Wall Street Journal reported a new SEC investigation into whether Nvidia disclosures misled investors. The board created a national security and export control oversight committee. Earnings beat and guidance rose, with no 10-Q filed with the release. The December House interview dates are now reported as agreed, and Muddy Waters disclosed a short with an expressly unverified identity question at its center.

The window brought the first official government account of the Megaspeed investigation. The Commerce and Justice Departments issued a joint statement setting out their timeline and putting the Justice Department in the lead on the criminal investigation, while making no allegation against Nvidia or Jensen Huang and saying nothing on the Entity List question. On the return question, reporting now has the board not considering bringing Huang back, the opposite direction from the comeback reporting in the record. President Trump and Vice President Vance both cast doubt on the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. In the Senate, the Commerce Committee's ranking member put four alleged export control failures in writing to Secretary Lutnick, and a Republican senator introduced a bill to force a listing decision on Megaspeed within 30 days. The shareholder case against Nvidia and Huang widened by amended complaint.

In this window the first government act in the case landed. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule closing the remote access channel at the center of the Megaspeed business model, and imposed a new destination license requirement covering Singapore and Malaysia, Megaspeed's two operating jurisdictions. The Straits Times reported the first known enforcement action in Indonesia linked to the case, a police search of Megaspeed's Indonesian subsidiary that found empty server racks and no chips. President Trump publicly welcomed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, in the opposite direction from his Treasury secretary's push for an outside chief executive.

In this window the succession fight split in public on the same Sunday shows that moved the congressional track. Jensen Huang has agreed to a closed-door interview with the three House committees, with no subpoena needed and the date still being discussed. A briefed Gang of Eight member said on the record that the intelligence community does not know whether Alice Huang was a witting asset. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent directed the board toward an outside chief executive and set it a 10-day deadline to answer on export-compliance culture, while the Financial Times reported Huang himself is discussing a comeback, with an ally war room lobbying for his return.

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

In this window the fight over the classified memo at the center of the case widened: the Washington Post reported the memo was Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recasting of a CIA report in more assertive terms, and CNN reported the CIA is not yet convinced the intercepts prove Alice Huang knowingly funneled information to Beijing. The Financial Times reported Nvidia carries directors and officers insurance that protects its directors personally and not the company, filings show a director sold about $946.6 million of stock in the weeks before the board inquiry opened, and Reuters reported Chinese AI firms are racing to reserve Nvidia powered capacity outside China before the remote rental loophole closes. South Korea said Nvidia has reconfirmed its 260,000 GPU supply plan after the resignation, Bill Ackman defended Huang on presumption of innocence grounds, and the first Sunday show booking for a case chair was announced for tomorrow.

Overnight, Reuters reported that Jensen Huang told Nvidia's own general counsel and chief marketing officer in writing that his interactions with Alice Huang and Megaspeed were standard business dealings, the House chairs' 8 p.m. deadline for his written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public, and a filings-based reconstruction put $5,353 million of Nvidia's formerly Singapore-billed revenue with China and Hong Kong headquartered buyers. Super Micro denied on the record that Megaspeed was ever its customer, a sitting administration official argued Huang should have been warned the way a congressman once was, and the street kept repricing the overhang: HSBC cut its target by more than half, and a billionaire holder said he will make no further investment in Nvidia without Huang.

Today the fight over the Megaspeed Entity List delay became an open cabinet split, the Commerce Secretary's own tenure came into question, Reuters documented the scale of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips, and the succession search moved in public for the first time: the board was reported to have approached an external candidate, then issued its first statement calling candidate speculation premature, while two major holders asked the board to slow the process down and keep Jensen Huang's return on the table. The 8 p.m. deadline for Huang's written acceptance of the December 1 interview passed with nothing public.

THE SUCCESSION SEARCH MOVES, THEN THE BOARD PUSHES BACK

Overnight, the House turned its request to Jensen Huang into an ultimatum with a deadline tonight, the Senate Banking subpoena threat was verified from the letter itself and shown to run to Huang only, Bloomberg published the first account of how the admission and the resignation decision actually happened, Malaysia opened its own official inquiry into the Megaspeed channel while its prime minister said there is no indication so far that chips were exported from Malaysia, and CNN's reporting reframed the Alice Huang spy question toward recruitment after access.

The first full day after Jensen Huang's resignation widened the case on every front at once. Huang agreed to testify before Congress, the Senate Banking Committee requested dated public hearings for Huang and for Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, the tax committees opened their own investigation with a records preservation demand, the Justice Department spoke on the record for the first time, Singapore published its full account of the Alice Huang investigation, and the channel record added two new end points, DeepSeek and Huawei.

THE TAX COMMITTEES OPEN AN INVESTIGATION

The case resolved overnight. Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, ending the board process that had built through the night: Semafor had reported some directors favored CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and Kress is the interim appointment in the release. The night also deepened the record behind the case, with the Wall Street Journal's account of the husband who introduced Huang to Alice Huang, Congress turning its fire on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Megaspeed's first public statement, and the analyst downgrade wave broadening before the announcement landed.

In twelve hours the case moved from congressional pressure to the boardroom. The New York Times reported a second extramarital relationship, this one with a direct report. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang, and Bloomberg reported a succession search is under way. The committees' 5 PM deadline for his answer on the November 18 briefing passed with no acceptance or alternative date reported, and the desk raised its exit estimate in this window.

Atlas Peak Research. Compiled from public reporting, company statements, and congressional and court records. Each edition covers twelve hours of the case and appears here in full.

items.body: 老黄离开后的英伟达三季度财报看点：本季大超预期下季及下一财年指引很强劲，对外新的投资担保谨慎，董事会明确不打算请回老黄。聊聊个人理解。 1、具体数字很多地方都能看到，只说关键点： 1）Vera Rubin开始正式交货、创造力英伟达历史上最快的爬坡记录，单季交付超过200亿美金，这个量级与公司本季约196亿美元的整体环比收入增量接近，说明新产品是增量来源，且新产品的交付本没有挤压原有产线的销售； 2）下一季指引1300亿美元，达到所有买方卖方的最高预期水平。 3）进一步上调了2028财年增长预期（本季是27财年第三季度），公司目前预计截至2028年1月的2028财年营收同比增长约75%，高于此前提出的70%以上增长目标。今年（2027财年）英伟达的营收应该能超过4200亿美金，那么明年（2028财年）按照75%的增速营收能超过7400亿美金。 4）公司三财季通过回购和分红向股东返还281亿美元。剩余股票回购授权约2273亿美元，要在28年之前完成，意味着未来五个季度单季平均回购450亿美金的股票，回购力度已经达到单季自由现金流的规模。 2、电话会议上临时CEO聊到几个关于产业的信息 1）OpenRouter上的周度Token使用量同比激增35倍，过去三个月内增长了3.5倍。智能体工作负载目前占据约80%的Token量。 自5月以来Token价格已下降近60%，这推动了Token使用量的加速增长和算力需求的扩张。也带动GPU租用价格跨代上涨——已有老一代GPU在多年期合同中以最高两倍的原价续约，而B300的租用费率自推出以来已上涨逾60%。 2）CPO路线快速推进，规模化生产已经启动。Lambda宣布了英伟达光子CPO交换机的首个量产部署，连接逾1万颗GB300 GPU。与公开插拔式光模块方案相比，英伟达光子交换机的能效提升5倍，可靠性提升15倍，延迟降低10%。三季度，英伟达的网络业务收入超过210亿美元。这可能是看到的对上游产业链最利好的一个信息。 3）Vera Rubin Ultra仍按计划于明年发布，Feynman将于2028年推出。 POD到货后即可直接连接部署，将上线时间从数月压缩至数周，大幅加快首次Token生成的时间。对于年收入规模达500亿美元的1吉瓦AI工厂而言，仅仅提前一个季度达到首次Token生成，就可能为运营商额外带来逾100亿美元的收入。 4）云行业积压订单目前已达2.5万亿美元，较三个月前的2万亿美元进一步增长。 3、资本生态 截至第三财季末英伟达的供应承诺从上一财季的2790亿美元增加至3900亿美元，主要与多年期内存采购有关。 此外公司云服务协议和数据中心租赁承诺合计达到1020亿美元，高于上一季度的740亿美元。 如果进一步计入股权投资、资本开支等项目，英伟达披露的未来各项承诺合计达到5180亿美元。 而相关融资担保敞口和Neocloud协议由公司另外列示： 1）披露最高1180亿美元的第三方融资担保敞口。最大的一笔涉及俄亥俄州SB Energy建设的数据中心园区。英伟达提供的相关担保最高达到1050亿美元，项目将建设约4.25吉瓦的数据中心容量，并通过长达20年的租赁安排为OpenAI提供基础设施。 2）公司还披露与新兴云服务商（Neoclouds）的相关承诺达到320亿美元。 关于“英伟达是否准备收缩客户融资”， Kress在会上发出了明确信号：英伟达在支持新兴云客户时将变得更加“克制和挑剔”。她表示公司正在“严格评估”各项投资、承诺和财务担保。 Kress详细划定了英伟达的担保底线： 如果（数据中心建设）开始了，但不幸的是他们被推迟了，或者在建设方面遇到了挑战，我们的担保就不再存在了。我们对其中大多数项目的担保，实际上是基于它们准备就绪的时候。 我的理解是：原有的仍在继续，但未来项目的筛选应该会更谨慎和严格。英伟达不再为早期的水泥建设或选址买单，只有当数据中心的土地、电力和外壳等基础设施真正就绪时，财务担保才会生效。 这向其实发出一个明确信号：部分企业是时候自力更生了。对于Neocloud来说，27年要为生存而战了。 4、关于老黄回归问题 董事会主席Harvey Jones在电话会明确表示董事会不打算恢复黄仁勋的CEO职务。他透露，董事会目前正同步考察内外部的CEO候选人，并表示“此次遴选将会全面而审慎”，在“找到真正合适的人选”前，公司绝不会仓促推进。 “先进芯片技术和国家安全形势正在改变英伟达的经营环境，而新任 CEO 必须能够妥善应对这些变化。” 虽然昨晚老黄也表态了回归的意愿，但是今年电话会的表态我们也要做好未来老黄不能回归的准备。 5、怎么看这份财报对市场的影响 1）短期内强劲财报和下季下一财年的指引会提振市场的情绪，短期内可能会带动市场一波反弹。 2）但中长期最大的考验还是如果老黄确定不能回归后，新的ceo能不能顶替上来。不然市场还是会对技术迭代的速度，产业生态支持力度心存疑虑。 本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易

items.title: https://t.co/JxTas8fyD4 $NVDA KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM NVIDIA’S Q3 FISCAL 2027 EARNINGS CALL NVIDIA’s results strengthen the outlook for AI infrastructure spending, but the more acti
items.body: https://t.co/JxTas8fyD4 $NVDA KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM NVIDIA’S Q3 FISCAL 2027 EARNINGS CALL NVIDIA’s results strengthen the outlook for AI infrastructure spending, but the more actionable conclusion is that economic benefits are becoming increasingly uneven across the supply chain. The strongest positive signals favor scarce memory, qualified substrates, advanced packaging, optical components and already-operational computing capacity. The clearest negatives affect thin-margin hardware buyers, infrastructure projects awaiting power or commissioning, and Chinese frontier-model developers facing tighter access restrictions. The increase in fiscal 2028 revenue-growth guidance from 70% to 75% supports continued investment, while NVIDIA’s rising commitments and customer-support arrangements show that financing and deployment readiness increasingly determine who captures that growth. Magnitude assessments below distinguish business-level exposure from consolidated earnings sensitivity; they do not imply specific share-price returns. Country labels identify issuers’ home markets. MEMORY: SUPPLIERS ARE CAPTURING ECONOMIC VALUE THAT NVIDIA IS TEMPORARILY ABSORBING (READ-THROUGH 1) Affected companies: Micron Technology (MU: US) and SK hynix (000660: South Korea). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High for memory earnings visibility and pricing durability, without sufficient disclosure to allocate NVIDIA’s commitments between suppliers. The strongest evidence is not simply NVIDIA’s revenue growth. Its CFO commentary states that supply commitments increased from $279 billion to $390 billion, “primarily related to the multi-year procurement of memory supply.” Scheduled fiscal 2028 supply commitments increased from $87 billion to $203 billion. Meanwhile, NVIDIA reaffirmed a gross-margin decline to 71%-72% in Q4 and explained that it was honoring existing customer purchase orders before revised pricing takes effect. This combination indicates that a meaningful portion of the AI system’s economic value is accruing upstream to scarce components. The transmission mechanism is stronger contracted demand, better production visibility, favorable product mix and pricing support for qualified memory suppliers. Micron’s disclosed Rubin-related products include HBM4 and SOCAMM2 memory for Vera platforms, extending its exposure beyond GPU-attached HBM. SK hynix’s October 28 results independently corroborate the contractual shift: agreements cover more than 50% of its 2027-2028 production capacity, with pricing mechanisms that reflect market conditions within negotiated ranges. The near-term catalyst is increased confidence in the duration of memory pricing and contracted demand, rather than an assumption that all $111 billion of incremental commitments becomes immediate supplier revenue. The longer-duration benefit is improved utilization and investment visibility into 2027-2028. The principal limitation is that long-term agreements do not eliminate pricing cyclicality, qualification risk or eventual capacity oversupply. Nevertheless, this is a stronger signal for memory profitability than a generic increase in AI capital expenditure. SUBSTRATES: CUSTOMER-SPECIFIC CAPACITY AGREEMENTS FAVOR IDENTIFIED SUPPLIERS, NOT THE ENTIRE GROUP EQUALLY (READ-THROUGH 2) Affected companies: Kinsus Interconnect Technology (3189: Taiwan) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150: South Korea). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Potentially high for Kinsus’s NVIDIA-related substrate business; moderate at Samsung Electro-Mechanics’s consolidated level. NVIDIA explicitly announced new substrate agreements with these companies. The accompanying November 17 supplier release states that Kinsus will expand advanced ABF substrate capacity dedicated to NVIDIA to more than 3.5x current levels. Production is expected to begin in the second half of calendar 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for Q3 2028. Samsung Electro-Mechanics amended its existing agreement to improve production capabilities at existing factories. These are identifiable commercial relationships rather than thematic exposure to semiconductor demand. Larger and more complex computing packages require qualified substrates with demanding routing, dimensional-stability and reliability characteristics. Dedicated capacity arrangements improve demand visibility and support capital investment in capabilities that cannot be substituted immediately. The distinction between existing-factory improvements and greenfield expansion matters. Samsung Electro-Mechanics potentially has a shorter operational path to incremental output, while Kinsus has a larger disclosed dedicated-capacity expansion but a later realization schedule. The 3.5x figure applies to NVIDIA-dedicated capacity, not Kinsus’s total revenue or earnings. The immediate trading catalyst is stronger confidence in customer allocation and the durability of advanced-substrate demand. The fundamental catalysts are equipment installation, customer qualification and utilization through 2027-2028. Initial depreciation, yield learning and ramp costs can precede meaningful earnings contributions. Treating the announcement as an immediate 3.5x earnings uplift would materially overstate its significance. FOUNDRY AND PACKAGING: NVIDIA IS FINANCING BOTTLENECK RELIEF, NOT DEMONSTRATING FOUNDRY DISINTERMEDIATION (READ-THROUGH 3) Affected companies: Amkor Technology (AMKR: US), ASE Technology Holding (3711: Taiwan), through wholly owned subsidiary Siliconware Precision Industries, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (2330: Taiwan). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High strategic significance for Amkor and SPIL’s advanced-packaging businesses; positive but less directly quantifiable at the consolidated TSMC and ASE levels. The call named SPIL and Amkor among NVIDIA’s expanding packaging partners. NVIDIA’s accompanying release specifies nearly $3 billion of previously announced Amkor agreements supporting Arizona and South Korean capacity, including prepayments. The new SPIL agreement includes multibillion-dollar funding and targets additional contracted advanced-packaging capacity by mid-2029. The transmission mechanism combines future service revenue with reduced external funding requirements. Customer prepayments can help suppliers build capacity before production revenue arrives, improving project financing and visibility. They are not immediate packaging revenue, and the nearly $3 billion Amkor figure includes agreements announced in July and October rather than an entirely new award on this call. The less obvious conclusion is that broader outsourced packaging participation does not establish a loss of TSMC’s advanced-node wafer business. NVIDIA’s November 17 release explicitly identifies TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS technologies in Vera Rubin and Vera CPU shipments. Additional assembly, interposer and testing capacity can relieve constraints around a growing platform without displacing the underlying foundry relationship. Near-term catalysts are funding, construction and qualification milestones. The largest disclosed SPIL packaging contribution is a 2028-2029 development rather than a near-term quarterly earnings event. Geographic diversification into the US and South Korea also has strategic value, although higher costs and ramp inefficiencies can delay profit conversion. OPTICAL COMPONENTS: CO-PACKAGED OPTICS SHIFTS VALUE TOWARD LASERS AND INTEGRATION RATHER THAN ELIMINATING OPTICS DEMAND (READ-THROUGH 4) Affected companies: Lumentum Holdings (LITE: US) and Coherent (COHR: US). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High strategic relevance to their data-center optics franchises; near-term earnings magnitude depends on product mix and shipment timing. NVIDIA reported networking revenue exceeding $21 billion, co-packaged-optics scale-out products in volume production and a production deployment connecting more than 10,000 GB300 GPUs. Management cited 5x better power efficiency, 15x higher reliability and 10% lower latency versus pluggable optics in the referenced configuration. The relevant supplier relationships are established. NVIDIA’s March announcements with Lumentum and Coherent included multibillion-dollar purchase commitments, capacity-access rights and $2 billion investments in each company. The agreements are nonexclusive. The current call therefore provides evidence of commercialization against an existing investment framework, rather than announcing those commitments again. The mechanism is greater demand for advanced laser components, optical networking products and package integration as bandwidth moves closer to switching silicon. Integrating optical functions does not remove the need to generate, transmit and receive optical signals. Consequently, a blanket negative view on optical suppliers because of CPO adoption would overlook the retained and potentially expanding upstream component opportunity. The near-term catalyst is evidence that CPO has progressed into production deployment. The longer-duration catalyst is broader adoption across 2027-2028 infrastructure generations. The call does not establish supplier allocations within the Lambda deployment or justify applying NVIDIA’s networking growth directly to either supplier’s revenue. It also does not support a blanket short of companies with pluggable-optics exposure, since product portfolios and retained content differ. CPU ARCHITECTURE: AGENTIC COMPUTING EXPANDS ARM’S OPPORTUNITY BEYOND GPU HOSTING (READ-THROUGH 5) Affected company: Arm Holdings (ARM: UK). Direction: Positive for the architecture and royalty opportunity. Magnitude: High strategic importance, but unquantified and likely more gradual at the consolidated earnings level. NVIDIA stated that agentic AI is driving CPU demand “far outstripping supply” and expects total CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028. Newly named Vera adopters included CoreWeave, Meta, Nscale and OpenAI, joining AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and other previously announced customers. Arm’s own technical commentary confirms that Vera uses NVIDIA-designed Olympus cores built on the Arm architecture. The mechanism is broader deployment of Arm-based processors for agent execution, code interpretation, retrieval, orchestration and scientific workloads. These functions generate CPU demand alongside accelerators rather than simply replacing CPU work with GPUs. The important distinction is between NVIDIA’s CPU revenue and Arm’s monetization. Arm does not receive the full selling price of a Vera processor, and custom Olympus cores should not be confused with NVIDIA purchasing a complete standard Arm CPU design. The opportunity is architecture licensing and royalty-bearing shipments under the applicable agreements, whose economics were not disclosed on the call. The near-term catalyst is adoption and shipment evidence supporting a larger data-center royalty base. The longer-duration shift is an expanding software ecosystem around Arm-based agent infrastructure. The evidence supports this architecture-level positive more strongly than it supports a quantified earnings short in Intel or AMD: additional CPU demand can expand the market even as suppliers compete for workload allocation. CONSUMER HARDWARE: THE SAME MEMORY CYCLE THAT BENEFITS SUPPLIERS CREATES A PRICING-AND-VOLUME TRAP FOR PC OEMS (READ-THROUGH 6) Affected company: HP Inc. (HPQ: US). Direction: Negative for underlying PC unit demand and margin flexibility. Magnitude: Material because Personal Systems is a large, thin-margin business, although the call does not establish an incremental earnings miss. NVIDIA’s CFO commentary states that higher memory and system prices continue to affect consumer PC demand. This is particularly informative because NVIDIA simultaneously reported strong workstation and physical-AI demand. Enterprise infrastructure strength should therefore not be interpreted as evidence of a uniform hardware recovery. HP’s latest reported q

external_articles.title: NVIDIA Corporation | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
Q3 strengthened the near-term earnings case; longer-duration risk transfer more visible

Q4 revenue is guided to $126.1 billion to $133.9 billion, excluding China Data Center compute revenue and including an additional week. Fiscal 2028 revenue growth rises to approximately 75% from 70%, off a higher fiscal 2027 base. Management reaffirmed adjusted gross margins of 71%-72% for Q4 and 72%-73% for fiscal 2028. Q4 adjusted operating expenses rise to about $10.7 billion. Executed price increases begin benefiting Q1 fiscal 2028; the fiscal 2027 adjusted tax-rate outlook is reaffirmed at 16%-18%.

Data Center revenue rose 21% sequentially to $107.6 billion, with hyperscale growth accelerating to 23%. Nearly $20 billion of initial-quarter Rubin revenue materially reduced near-term transition risk. The operating-profit beat was predominantly revenue-driven, not expense restraint. Licensed Hopper shipments to China contributed $2.4 billion against guidance that assumed none, so the full headline beat should not be treated as recurring non-China upside. Rubin also substituted for the preceding architecture; its contribution was comparable to the entire sequential Data Center increase.

Free cash flow reached $43.777 billion, approximately 67.5% of adjusted net income; federal cash-tax timing contributed to the recovery. Receivables rose to $81.0 billion and DSO to 64 days from 60, reflecting Rubin shipment timing and extended payment terms for certain investment-grade customers. Inventory also grew faster than revenue. Earnings improvement was overwhelmingly operational rather than repurchase-driven. Fiscal 2027 non-GAAP measures now include stock-based compensation, and historical comparisons were restated; older unreconciled adjusted results would distort growth.

The Q4 and fiscal 2028 margin ranges were already communicated in August, not newly deteriorating forecasts. NVIDIA is honoring existing purchase orders before revised pricing takes effect, creating a lag between component-cost inflation and contractual recovery. This differs from disclosed price cuts to defend share, but some cost pressure remains absorbed. Q3 expense underspending partly reflected nonrecurring-engineering timing and should not be annualized. The near-term earnings trajectory is less explosive than the revenue guidance initially suggests.

Supply commitments reached $390 billion, cloud-service and data-center lease commitments $102 billion, and maximum gross guarantee exposure $118 billion. These are not equivalent debt or immediate cash requirements. Approximately $21.1 billion of net financial liquidity excludes leases and contingent obligations, while capital expenditures and related principal payments consumed approximately $4.48 billion. Neocloud commitments activate after financing, deployment and acceptance, but post-completion operating and credit exposure remains.

Q3 ended before Huang’s November 12 resignation, so the reported quarter does not establish unchanged execution without the founder. Remote-access export controls can affect non-China customers and infrastructure redeployability. Q3 strengthened the near-term earnings case while making longer-duration risk transfer more visible. Exceptional product execution did not eliminate uncertainty around leadership, regulation, customer financing or infrastructure returns.

Micron (MU), SK hynix (000660) | Positive | High for memory earnings visibility and pricing durability

Supply commitments rose from $279 billion to $390 billion, primarily for multi-year memory procurement. NVIDIA is absorbing component inflation while honoring existing customer orders, supporting memory suppliers’ contracted demand and pricing. SK hynix agreements cover more than 50% of 2027-2028 capacity. Supplier allocations are undisclosed, and the commitments are not immediate supplier revenue; qualification and eventual oversupply remain risks. Micron’s Rubin-related products include HBM4 and SOCAMM2.

Nebius (NBIS) | Negative | High for near-term revenue timing and capital efficiency

Nebius moved expected 2026 revenue to the low end of its $3.0 billion-$3.4 billion range, raised capital-expenditure guidance to approximately $27 billion and shifted its year-end run-rate milestone into February. More GPU supply does not resolve power, commissioning or acceptance delays, leaving capital deployed before revenue activates. Neocloud commitments require financing, operation and acceptance. Contracts remain in place, and qualifying Q3 prepayments exceeded associated capital expenditures: the negative is timing, not a blanket funding crisis.

CoreWeave (CRWV) | Positive | High operating relevance, with a substantially more qualified implication for equity cash flows

Certain Hopper renewals reached up to 2x original prices, while B300 rental rates rose more than 60%. Existing operational sites can monetize scarce compute, supporting fleet revenue durability and residual values. The increases are not fleet-wide, and fixed-price contracts reprice only when permitted. CoreWeave’s adjusted net loss underscores that strong equipment economics do not eliminate financing needs or depreciation.

Lumentum (LITE), Coherent (COHR) | Positive | High strategic relevance to their data-center optics franchises; near-term earnings magnitude depends on product mix and shipment timing

A production deployment connecting more than 10,000 GB300 GPUs demonstrates CPO commercialization. Optical integration shifts demand toward lasers and package integration rather than eliminating optical signals. Existing nonexclusive supplier agreements include multibillion-dollar purchase commitments and $2 billion investments in each company. The call does not establish supplier allocations or justify applying NVIDIA’s networking growth directly to either supplier’s revenue.

Prepared from the company's earnings release and earnings call transcript. Figures as reported by the company. For information only. Not investment advice.

items.title: https://t.co/ajH7wS47kM $POWL KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM POWELL INDUSTRIES’ FISCAL Q4 2026 EARNINGS CALL Powell’s November 17, 2026 earnings call supports continued strength in electri
items.body: https://t.co/ajH7wS47kM $POWL KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM POWELL INDUSTRIES’ FISCAL Q4 2026 EARNINGS CALL Powell’s November 17, 2026 earnings call supports continued strength in electrical equipment, power-generation infrastructure, LNG equipment and specialized construction. The most important signal is not simply expanding demand: manufacturing capacity is translating into revenue while underlying margins remain resilient. However, the call also exposes significant differences in economic quality across the investment chain. Standardized data-center equipment carries greater scope-change risk than traditional engineered industrial projects, skilled labor is becoming a more important execution constraint, and exceptionally strong equipment-manufacturer cash flow should not be extrapolated to installation contractors. The strongest positive implications concern earnings durability through 2027 and 2028; the strongest negative implications concern the permanence of scarcity-driven pricing, fixed-price execution economics and working-capital requirements. Most relevant peers had already reported their September-quarter results, making Powell’s disclosures incremental corroboration rather than an advance signal of those completed quarters. Magnitudes below describe fundamental exposure and the incremental information supplied by this call, not predicted share-price movements. Countries denote corporate domicile. ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT: UNDERLYING MARGIN STRENGTH IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN THE HEADLINE REVENUE BEAT (READ-THROUGH 1) Affected companies: Eaton Corporation (ETN: Ireland) and Schneider Electric (SU: France). Direction and magnitude: Positive. The underlying earnings exposure is substantial, while the incremental information from Powell is moderately positive because both companies had already reported strong demand. The read-through is strongest for North American power distribution, switchgear and associated electrical systems, rather than every business within these diversified groups. Powell’s supporting evidence is unusually strong. Revenue increased 33% in Q4, commercial and other industrial revenue increased 179%, and utility revenue increased 22%. More importantly, annual gross margin increased from 29.4% to 31.3% despite favorable project-closeout contributions declining from approximately 185 basis points to 150 basis points. Excluding those disclosed benefits, the underlying margin improved by approximately 225 basis points. Metcalf stated that Powell was “exiting the backlog at about a 30% clip,” consistent with the margin embedded in remaining work. Management also reported pricing at or above inflationary benchmarks. The transmission mechanism is higher factory utilization combined with sustained price realization. Strong electrical-infrastructure spending fills production schedules, improves fixed-cost absorption and reduces the need to discount capacity. Powell’s results indicate that customers’ urgency is still translating into favorable equipment economics even as manufacturers expand production. This reduces the risk that strong order books conceal an imminent deterioration in realized margins. Eaton’s November 3 results provide independent confirmation: Electrical Americas organic sales increased 22%, rolling 12-month organic orders increased 39%, and backlog increased 33%. That segment generated approximately $4.2 billion of Eaton’s $8.9 billion quarterly revenue, making the exposure material at group level. Schneider’s October results likewise described strong Energy Management performance, electrical-distribution demand and increasing visibility into 2027 and 2028. Powell therefore reinforces an existing industry pattern rather than establishing an isolated company-specific improvement. The qualification is that Powell’s gross margin cannot be transferred directly to Eaton’s segment operating margin or Schneider’s adjusted profitability. Product mix, services, purchased components and accounting differ. Powell’s 34.9% quarterly gross margin also included 230 basis points of favorable closeouts and is not the appropriate industry baseline. Near-term trading catalyst: Greater confidence in order conversion and margin resilience during the next reporting cycle, particularly if peers maintain price realization while increasing output. The call is more supportive of earnings durability than of an immediate, mechanically quantifiable EPS upgrade. Longer-duration fundamental implication: Electrical suppliers capable of expanding qualified output without sacrificing execution should sustain higher earnings power through 2027 and 2028. The strongest beneficiaries combine manufacturing capacity with applications engineering, customer qualification and integrated controls, rather than relying exclusively on equipment shortages. ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT: STANDARDIZED DATA-CENTER GROWTH DESERVES A DIFFERENT VALUATION FROM CUSTOM INDUSTRIAL BACKLOG (READ-THROUGH 2) Affected companies: Eaton Corporation (ETN: Ireland) and Schneider Electric (SU: France). Direction and magnitude: Negative for assumptions that current delivery premiums and backlog certainty are permanent. The immediate earnings implication is limited; the potential medium-term valuation effect is moderate for overlapping configurable electrical-equipment businesses. This is not evidence of current industry-wide cancellations or a near-term short thesis. Powell explicitly differentiated data-center applications from its traditional business, describing them as “much more standard electrical applications.” Asked about cancellation risk, Cope stated, “The risk probably does go up because it’s a lot less engineering.” He acknowledged quantity changes and cancellations within programs, although work had generally been reallocated across phases, designs or campuses rather than producing a material net reduction in backlog. The competitive evidence is equally important. Cope said early data-center wins were driven by “capacity and availability.” Powell is now developing configure-to-order production lines, expanding customer relationships and committing to faster delivery. Its footprint increased more than 20% during fiscal 2026, with another approximately 275,000-square-foot facility expected online in fiscal Q3 2027. The transmission mechanism has 2 distinct components. First, standardized designs generally require less customer-specific engineering, potentially making quantities and suppliers easier to change before delivery. A backlog dollar supported primarily by a delivery reservation is not necessarily equivalent to a deeply engineered industrial project with substantial committed customization. Second, additional qualified capacity can weaken the scarcity component of pricing as customers obtain more delivery alternatives. Powell’s own evolution from an availability-driven entrant toward repeatable production is evidence that competition can intensify in these applications. Eaton and Schneider compete in overlapping electrical-distribution markets, but their actual cancellation protections and customer commitments cannot be inferred from Powell’s contracts. Their installed bases, product breadth, automation and services can also defend customer relationships. The high-conviction conclusion is that standardized hardware growth should not automatically receive the same durability assumptions as complex engineered systems or recurring services. It is not that either peer has already suffered an undisclosed deterioration. Near-term trading catalyst: Changes in order conversion, delivery lead times, price realization or customer rescheduling disclosures. A falling backlog-conversion percentage should be assessed alongside absolute scheduled revenue; longer project duration alone does not establish weakening demand. Longer-duration fundamental implication: During 2027 and 2028, valuation differentiation should increasingly depend on how much profitability comes from enduring technical differentiation versus temporary delivery scarcity. The negative implication is greatest for extrapolated scarcity premiums, not for the existence of substantial electrical demand. Powell’s expansion is too small to establish industry oversupply, but it weakens the assumption that current competitive conditions remain unchanged indefinitely. POWER GENERATION AND GRID EQUIPMENT: ELECTRICAL BOTTLENECKS SUPPORT A MULTIYEAR INVESTMENT CYCLE, NOT JUST A DATA-CENTER HARDWARE CYCLE (READ-THROUGH 3) Affected companies: GE Vernova (GEV: United States) and Baker Hughes (BKR: United States). Direction and magnitude: Positive, with high fundamental relevance to GE Vernova’s Power and Electrification businesses and meaningful relevance to Baker Hughes’ industrial power-generation activities. Powell provides moderate incremental confirmation of demand duration, not a new attributable turbine order. The supporting call evidence extends beyond the $85 million data-center award. Powell reported 34% growth in utility backlog and described demand as supported by “structurally undersupplied power generation and grid capacity.” Cope emphasized a substantial gap between generation capacity and grid requirements. Data-center customers continued to prioritize speed, while Powell’s overall backlog visibility extended through fiscal 2028 and beyond. The precise transmission mechanism is complementary infrastructure spending. Switchgear and power-control systems distribute and protect electricity; they cannot create generation capacity or eliminate transmission constraints. Sustained spending on electrical distribution therefore supports demand for the generation, grid connection, protection and control equipment required to make that infrastructure productive. Where conventional utility delivery cannot meet development schedules, dedicated generation can create an additional equipment requirement rather than simply shifting the timing of switchgear purchases. GE Vernova’s October 28 disclosures independently establish the relevant exposure. Power revenue was approximately $6.1 billion and Electrification revenue approximately $3.9 billion. Gas-equipment backlog plus slot-reservation agreements reached 122 GW, comprising 64 GW of backlog and 58 GW of reservations. Those categories should not be conflated: reservations provide commercial visibility but are not identical to firm equipment backlog. Baker Hughes’ October results disclosed specific U.S. AI-related power-generation awards representing approximately 1.1 GW and another approximately 500 MW. These verified awards make the dedicated-generation exposure concrete. They do not establish that Baker Hughes supplies Powell’s unnamed projects or that Powell’s latest order represents incremental business beyond awards already disclosed by Baker Hughes. The important counterpoint is order lumpiness. GE Vernova’s Electrification organic orders declined 9% against a large prior-year comparison, even as book-to-bill remained approximately 1.4x and equipment backlog expanded. Powell’s utility strength supports the underlying investment cycle, but it does not justify assuming uninterrupted quarterly order acceleration across the sector. Near-term trading catalyst: Conversion of generation reservations into firm orders, delivery-slot commitments and stronger evidence of equipment throughput. Powell’s call is supportive of those commercial opportunities but is not itself a contract announcement for either company. Longer-duration fundamental implication: Equipment deliveries expand the installed base available for maintenance, upgrades and services. The effect therefore extends beyond initial capital-equipment revenue. Cross-portfolio diversification should nevertheless be assessed carefully: positions in power equipment, dedicated generation and data-center electrical systems can share the same ultimate customer-spending driver despite different sector classifications. LNG AND INDUSTRIAL GAS EQUIPMENT: THE STRONGE

external_articles.title: Powell Industries, Inc. | Atlas Peak Research
external_articles.body:
Substantially stronger productive capacity, profitability and revenue visibility

No formal fiscal 2027 revenue or EPS range was issued. Management supports sustaining approximately 31.3% full-year gross margin, not a floor; facility commissioning could cause a productivity air pocket. Approximately $1.3 billion of backlog is scheduled for fiscal 2027 conversion. Fiscal Q1 revenue likely declines sequentially on seasonality. The leased facility is now expected in fiscal Q3 2027, versus late Q2 or early Q3 previously. The $15 million to $20 million capital-spending indication is incremental, not total. The greenfield facility remains unapproved.

Revenue exceeded consensus by 18.3% and gross profit by 33.7%. Commercial and other industrial revenue grew 179%, led by data centers, while utility revenue grew 22%; petrochemicals declined 49%. Management attributed acceleration to added capacity, with "No unusuals." Operating income reached $100.6 million as operating margin rose from 21.2% to 25.3%. The quarter demonstrated genuine underlying improvement rather than an earnings result driven predominantly by accounting benefits.

The 34.9% quarterly gross margin included 230 basis points of favorable closeouts. Most earnings improvement originated in operations; higher net interest income contributed $2.2 million and other income $1.5 million. Nonrecurring legal and professional expenses were not quantified, preventing a defensible adjustment. Quarterly operating cash flow of $239 million benefited substantially from customer milestones. Payments before production finance obligations to purchase materials, pay labor and deliver equipment, rather than representing completed economic performance.

Annual gross margin rose from 29.4% to 31.3% even as closeout benefits fell from approximately 185 to 150 basis points. Excluding those benefits, underlying margin improved approximately 225 basis points. Management described backlog margins at about 30%. The low-30% outlook carries execution-dependent upside and transitional downside. Stable pricing is commercial resilience, not complete insulation from future cost changes. Skilled labor, supplier availability and facility commissioning increasingly determine execution. Demand availability is no longer the principal investment debate; earnings durability and productive capacity are.

Cash and short-term investments of $860.8 million and no financial debt provide resilience, but customer-funded cash is not automatically excess capital. The expanded credit facility supports commercial letters of credit. Fiscal 2026 capital expenditures were $18.5 million; leased expansion also creates future rental obligations. Approximately $1.3 billion of backlog is scheduled to convert in fiscal 2027, unchanged from the prior rolling-window disclosure. Data-center configure-to-order programs carry higher cancellation risk. Customer concentration remains unresolved, and reallocation across campuses can preserve bookings while changing timing and working-capital needs.

Quarterly orders of $710 million included a $250 million LNG award and an $85 million data-center award. LNG bookings totaled approximately $350 million, demonstrating activity beyond the principal project. The largest LNG order spans approximately 3 years and carries margins broadly consistent with the backlog. Its benefits are scale, utilization and scheduling visibility, not a disclosed pricing step-change.

Eaton (ETN), Schneider Electric (SU) | Positive | Substantial underlying earnings exposure; moderately positive incremental information

Higher factory utilization and sustained price realization support North American distribution and switchgear earnings. Powell's annual underlying gross margin improved approximately 225 basis points as closeout contributions declined. Eaton's Electrical Americas organic sales rose 22%, corroborating the pattern. Powell adds moderately positive information to already-reported strength, not a mechanically quantifiable EPS upgrade. Its gross margin cannot be transferred directly to peer profitability.

GE Vernova (GEV), Baker Hughes (BKR) | Positive | High fundamental relevance to GEV Power and Electrification; meaningful to BKR industrial power generation

Switchgear cannot create generation capacity or remove transmission constraints. Powell's utility backlog grew 34%, supporting complementary spending on generation, grid connection and controls. GE Vernova's gas-equipment backlog plus reservations reached 122 GW, but reservations are not firm backlog. Baker Hughes disclosed AI-related generation awards. Powell corroborates demand duration, not an attributable turbine order or evidence that either company supplies its unnamed projects.

Quanta Services (PWR), MYR Group (MYRG) | Positive | High potential operating relevance for exposed businesses; moderate incremental information

Expanding equipment output can release installation, integration and energization work while increasing the value of qualified labor. Powell attributed approximately 27% sequential revenue growth to capacity, not unusual timing. Quanta's $63.7 billion backlog demonstrates broad exposure; MYR described customers securing labor and materials into 2029 and 2030. Benefits depend on project selection and productivity; manufacturer revenue does not mechanically predict contractors' following-quarter sales. Permitting, civil works and customer schedules remain independent constraints.

MYR Group (MYRG) | Negative | Potentially material effects on free cash flow and project profitability

Equipment suppliers can receive milestones before production while contractors fund payroll and materials before collection. MYR's quarterly operating cash flow fell to approximately $46 million from $96 million, primarily on billing and payment timing. Increased fixed-price work adds wage and productivity exposure. This is not a demand downgrade or solvency concern; Quanta's approximately $1.2 billion quarterly free cash flow counters sector-wide extrapolation. Temporary billing delays can reverse; MYR's recent margins improved.

Prepared from the company's earnings release and earnings call transcript. Figures as reported by the company. For information only. Not investment advice.

items.title: I spoke with some friends at $NVDA today. They seemed to think Jensen might be back soon!👀 I also asked how work has been since Jensen stepped down. They said executives at the VP
items.body: I spoke with some friends at $NVDA today. They seemed to think Jensen might be back soon!👀 I also asked how work has been since Jensen stepped down. They said executives at the VP level and above haven’t been joining regular work meetings as often, apparently because they’re tied up in other meetings, but everyday work seems to be continuing without any problems. I’ve heard that even as NVIDIA has grown, its individual teams still operate with the speed and agility of startups. Maybe that culture is showing its strength in a situation like this. I asked whether employees were doing anything to support Jensen’s return. They said there was nothing official, but they had signed a petition calling for him to come back, and many employees were also voicing their support through unofficial posts. At least among the people around them, they said no one was against his return. I don’t know how this will unfold, but as long as he hasn’t broken the law, I really hope he comes back to NVIDIA.

items.body: $NVDA $MU $SNDK $LITE He @JensenHuang doesn't comprehend that he was managing other people's money in a public vehicle. There is a fiduciary responsibility, and a burden of care, that goes with that honor. The SEC is now investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. --------------------- (Wall Street Journal) -- The Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Nvidia, whose star chief executive Jensen Huang recently resigned after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an employee, according to people familiar with the matter. The civil investigation adds to the crisis facing Nvidia, whose shares have fallen more than 10% since Huang was ousted. The focus of the investigation couldn't immediately be learned but includes whether the company's disclosures misled investors, some of the people said, Just weeks ago, Nvidia was a stock-market darling at the center of the booming artificial-intelligence trade and the most valuable company in the world. But now it has faced questions from investors about its disclosures related to Huang's affairs and its sales of its chips in Asia. Nvidia had denied earlier this year that Jensen Huang had an unusual or unexpected relationship with Alice Huang, then an executive at the Singapore-based data company Megaspeed who U.S. intelligence officials believe is working for China's intelligence services. Megaspeed was one of several companies using Nvidia chips to set up AI data centers in Southeast Asia and suspected of diverting some of the products to China. It had been under investigation by the Commerce Department since late 2024. The Justice Department is now leading multiple investigations involving Alice Huang, The Wall Street Journal has reported. Nvidia last year changed how it discloses international chip sales, eliminating a disclosure that showed its sales to Singapore, where Megaspeed was based. Since the Huang relationship was disclosed, Nvidia's business in Asia has been in the spotlight. Congress has called for investigations and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this week openly questioned whether Nvidia knowingly sold powerful chips to China to lift its earnings. "What was the culture at Nvidia and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said. "I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel." "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia," Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely."
